compute.note: Parameters: 64 from the method string (high confidence); the circuit code builds 64 one-parameter gates (SU2_symmetrized._get_dimerizarion_layers: range(1) x 4 shifts x (8 + 8) pairs), which reproduces it. Iterations: 2000 = 1000 natural-gradient steps without symmetry projection, then 1000 continuing with the 128-element projector (n_iter default 1000; main.py is called twice and passes only lr). As published, Optimizer.optimize() ends with "return res.x" on the circuit object, which has no attribute x, so the first call exits with an AttributeError and "&&" would skip the symmetric run; the step counts are therefore what the code intends, not what it can be shown to have run, hence confidence low. Samples: none; the method string says exact gradients on a state vector. The code has no exact branch that main.py reaches: it draws binomial estimates with the default 2^36 shots (--log2samples default 36), which is exact to about 4e-6 relative. Provenance: the value entered VarBench in 5d1ebf9 (2022-11-11, Nikita Astrakhantsev); the program was added to methods in 6887677 (2024-08-10) ("wip: added the VQE simulator"; next commit "VQE simulator: dusted-off version runs"), so it is a later reconstruction. The VarBench SM (arXiv:2302.04919 Sec. S3 D) describes the ansatz and the natural-gradient update but no step count. verified.note: Script runs main.py --j2=0.2 --lattice=square4x4 twice (--symmetry=0, then --symmetry=1 continuing from the logged parameters) with the default 2^36 shots (exact to ~4e-6 relative): HeisenbergSquare = sum (sigma.sigma + 1) over 2N NN + J2 x 2N NNN bonds, energy_renorm removed, i.e. Pauli J1-J2 without shift on the square4x4 (4x4 torus), PBC, S^z = 0 singlet; 64 gates = SU2_symmetrized (4 shifts x 16 pairs). The number the program prints is the exact state-vector energy <psi|H P|psi>/<psi|P|psi> of the circuit state (observables.py L196-200, '{:.7f}'), deterministic. Variance 0.0277 within the Bhatia-Davis bound (E-E0)(Emax-E) = 5.034e-2 (ratio 0.550; E0 = the ED row, Emax = 38.4 the ferromagnet). Caveat for reproduction: as committed, the first main.py call ends in AttributeError (optimizers.py L644 'return res.x' on the circuit returned at L300), so '&&' skips the symmetric stage; the value (5d1ebf9 2022-11-11) predates the program. History: entered 5d1ebf9 (2022-11-11, Nikita, 'Add files via upload'); unchanged since; code link added 5285adc (2024-08-12). Holds the instance's best variational bound (is_record).

corrections.reason: Whether an energy was sampled is read from the source, per row (ruling 2, 2026-09-30). The number the program prints is the exact statevector expectation of the circuit state, <psi|H P|psi>/<psi|P|psi> (observables.py L196-200, '{:.7f}'); the 2^14 shots per parameter estimate only the gradient and the metric (the shot-sampled circuit.energy of circuits.py L398 enters only the gradient and a local list in optimizers.py L281). The VarBench SM agrees (arXiv:2302.04919v2 Sec. S3 D: the shots measure the gradient and metric matrix elements), and so does the uploader's label on the 4 x 6 twin, 'Ns = 2^14 per par, statevector'. A deterministic energy needs no sigma (RULES.md 6); the method string's fallback read '2^14 samples' as a sampled energy. Caveat: the committed program is a 2024 reconstruction of the 2022 runs' code. This row is above the exact-gradient row (-39.6712875), so no record changes here.
